questions.questionText: Figure 6 shows the average revenue (AR), marginal revenue (MR) and marginal cost (MC) curves of a train-operating firm for peak-time and off-peak passengers. It also shows the price (P1) that all passengers currently pay. The train-operating firm introduces price discrimination to maximise profits. What is the effect on consumer surplus?
options: Falls for both off-peak and peak-time passengers
Falls for off-peak passengers and rises for peak-time passengers
Falls for peak-time passengers and rises for off-peak passengers
Rises for both off-peak and peak-time passengers

questions.questionText: Explain the likely impact on consumer surplus and producer surplus as an industry moves away from a competitive market structure to one that is dominated by a few large firms.

Figure 5 shows the average revenue (AR), marginal revenue (MR) and marginal cost (MC) curves for an industry which was perfectly competitive but is now a monopoly. The cost and revenue curves remain unchanged. Which of the following areas shows the total deadweight loss of consumer and producer surplus resulting from the structure of the industry changing from perfect competition to monopoly?

To reduce pollution, the city council pays bus companies to provide bus travel free of charge. As a result of this policy, consumer surplus will increase by the area
Explain how the imposition of a tax on a good or service affects both consumer surplus and producer surplus.
